chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from al-Ala', from al-Fudayl, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked: A man repudiates his child, yet he has acknowledged him. He said: If the child is from a free woman, he is lashed with fifty lashes, the penalty of a male slave; and if the child is from a female slave, there is no penalty upon him. The meaning in this report is that we should assume it is a mistake by the narrator, because the first report is consistent with the apparent meaning of the Quran and the reports we have presented in the first chapter, and this report is anomalous, so it is not objected against what we said with a similar one.
ai.seo_question: What is the punishment for repudiating an acknowledged child in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this report from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the specific distinction between a free and slave mother for the penalty of repudiation is analyzed as a likely *wahm* (narrator's error) or *shadh* (anomaly) because it contradicts the apparent meaning of the Quran and established precedents. Shaykh al-Tusi highlights this to demonstrate the methodology of reconciling conflicting reports by prioritizing those aligned with the Quranic text and stronger evidentiary chains.
